newsitem.title: USA: Missouri unemployment rises to 4.1 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Missouri unemployment rises to 4.1 pct in June.

text.p: Missouri's unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.1 percent in June, up from 3.8 percent in May, the labor and industrial relations department reported Friday.

The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped one percentage point to 3.9 percent, the lowest it has been since the department began calculating data with the current method in 1978, the department reported.
Nonfarm payroll employment showed little change in the month. The construction and the amusement and recreation services sectors posted seasonal gains, while other industries saw seasonal declines.
State and local government employment declined as did private educational services and related foodservice industries.

Nonfarm payroll employment has increased 47,000 jobs over the past year and construction has shown a slight increase as well. Manufacturing showed a slight decline with gains in the durable goods industries offset by losses in nondurable goods.

Service industries have grown by 46,300 jobs since June 1996 with gains in local government, business services, amusement and recreation services, banks and other depository institutions, automobile repair and health services.
